newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Safrica Mondi workers shot at during strike.
newsitem.headline: Safrica Mondi workers shot at during strike.

text.p: Non-striking workers at the paper division of South Africa's Mondi, a subsidiary of Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd, have been shot at and stoned, the company said on Tuesday.
A Mondi driver, Bafana Zwane, was shot dead in his home on Monday night after finishing work, the company said in a statement.
Police said they suspect the killing was related to the wage strike which has lasted almost a month at Mondi's Merebank mill where he worked.
Mondi said shots had been fired at Zwane's home three weeks ago and "the homes of other non-striking Mondi workers were also shot at and stoned."
The incidents, especially the murder, if proved to be strike related, could influence the strike and labour bargaining countrywide, the company warned.
A spokesman for the Paper, Printing, Wood and Allied Workers' Union said the union distanced itself from the murder and intimidation.
"We don't condone any acts of violence or intimidation. People involved in these acts from any side need to be brought to book," Mhlaba Mkhize told Reuters.
He said negotiations between the union and management had deadlocked and there was no point in holding further meetings.

"The attitude of the strikers is hardening and they are saying they will stay out until their demands are met. Our offer of an eleven percent increase has fallen away and we have gone back to our 14.75 percent demand," Mkhize said.
Mondi said the dispute had been referred to the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration, but the process had failed.
"The mill is in production with all five of its paper machines running," it said, adding that about 550 out of its 1,320 workers were on strike.
Management was not immediately available for comment on how the strike was affecting production.
